identity.name: Brown FK
identity.chemical_class: Synthetic sulfonated azo dye mixture (food colour)

function.mechanism: Mixture of azo dyes that imparts brown colour through visible-light absorption by azo chromophores; historically used to colour smoked kippers.

adi.basis: EFSA (2010) cited historical SCF ADI of 0.15 mg/kg bw/day but concluded it could not confirm safety due deficiencies in the toxicity database.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA Panel was unable to conclude on the safety of Brown FK (E154) because the available toxicity dataset was deficient.

fda.cfr_citation: 21 CFR 70.3(f); 21 CFR 70.5; Title 21 Parts 73/74/81 (no Brown FK listing found in Title 21 XML search)

adi.basis: Latest JECFA evaluation (1986): NO ADI ALLOCATED; previous temporary ADI in 1985 was 0-0.075 mg/kg bw/day.

notable_bans: European Union: E154 not identified in the current consolidated Annex II Union list text checked.
United States: Brown FK not identified in eCFR Title 21 colour-additive listings reviewed.

concerns.summary: Older studies reported mutagenicity/genotoxicity findings for Brown FK or related components in bacterial systems and in assays using rat excreta after oral dosing.
JECFA toxicology monograph described some metabolites as cardiotoxic and reported dose-related myopathy/pigment deposition findings in animal studies at higher doses.
Long-term animal studies had uncertainty and data gaps (including incomplete lower-dose histopathology), leading EFSA to state it could not conclude on safety.

no_concern_confirmed: JECFA comments noted no clear increase in tumour incidence and no adverse reproductive/teratogenic findings in reviewed studies, but overall data quality limitations remained.

populations: Children (high-percentile consumers of smoked fish products)
adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA 2010 refined exposure reached up to 0.14 mg/kg bw/day in children at P95, close to the historical SCF ADI of 0.15 mg/kg bw/day.

risk_assessment.rationale: Authoritative reassessments did not confirm safety (EFSA non-conclusion; JECFA NO ADI ALLOCATED), while older toxicology indicates plausible genotoxic/cardiotoxic concerns and current major-jurisdiction positive-list support was not found.
key_factors: EFSA (2010) unable to conclude on safety due toxicity-data deficiencies
JECFA latest status: NO ADI ALLOCATED
No Brown FK listing identified in reviewed EU/US current legal listings
Older genotoxic and cardiotoxic-related animal/mechanistic concern signals
